title: Changes that change nothing
prompt: The CRM sends an update for every edit, including a renamed account or an update that changes nothing. The history should only get a new version when a column in `TRACKED` changes. Write `apply_batch(changes)`.
rules: Use each account's newest change in the batch, by `sequence`.
An update applies only if at least one `TRACKED` column differs from the account's current version. Other updates are ignored: the current version stays open as it is. These columns are never empty.
A delete always closes the current version. A change for an account with no current version adds a new version, unless it's a delete.

Applying a change closes the account's current version (`effective_to` becomes the change's `changed_at`, `is_current` false) and, unless it's a delete, adds the change as a new version: `effective_from` is `changed_at`, `effective_to` NULL, `is_current` true. Every other version stays as it is. Don't change `start_history` or `solve`.
hints: Join the newest changes to the current versions on `account_id` (a left join, so new accounts stay), renaming the current version's tracked columns so you can compare them.
OR together one `!=` per tracked column. A delete's row is the account as it was, so it differs in nothing: let deletes through on their own.
After the join an account with no current version has NULL in the current version's columns. Select the change's own columns again before the MERGE and the append.
starter:
import shutil

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

PATH = "/tmp/crm/dim_accounts"
COLS = ["account_id", "account_name", "industry", "country", "segment", "account_owner", "credit_limit", "created_on", "is_active"]
TRACKED = ["segment", "account_owner", "credit_limit", "is_active"]


def start_history(accounts):
    # The history starts with each snapshot account, valid from the snapshot. Don't change this.
    shutil.rmtree(PATH, ignore_errors=True)  # start from an empty folder on every run
    (accounts
        .withColumn("effective_from", F.lit("2026-01-01 00:00:00").cast("timestamp"))
        .withColumn("effective_to", F.lit(None).cast("timestamp"))
        .withColumn("is_current", F.lit(True))
        .write.format("delta").save(PATH))


def apply_batch(changes):
    # Apply the batch to the history at PATH as type 2, ignoring changes that leave every TRACKED column as it is.
    pass

def solve(accounts, customer_cdc):
    start_history(accounts)
    apply_batch(customer_cdc)
    return spark.read.format("delta").load(PATH)
explanation: Cut the batch to each account's newest change, then left-join the current versions, with their tracked columns renamed. Keep a change when it's a delete, when the account had no current version, or when any tracked column differs: `(F.col("segment") != F.col("cur_segment")) | ...`. Apply only those, with the usual MERGE that closes the current version and an append of the new ones. ACC-0005's rename changes no tracked column, so its snapshot version stays open. A delete carries the account as it was, so comparing columns alone would never let it through, and an inner join would drop ACC-0006 and ACC-0007, which the history doesn't have yet. Leave out `is_active` and ACC-0004's deactivation is lost.
